landmarks.name: CEPSUM
facts: It is the university's sports centre, home of the Carabins.
It hosted fencing at the 1976 Summer Olympics.

landmarks.name: HEC Montréal – Édifice Côte-Sainte-Catherine
facts: Its business school was the first school of management in Canada.
That school was founded in 1907 by the city's Board of Trade.

landmarks.name: Pavillon de la faculté de l'aménagement
Faculté de musique de Université de Montréal
Pavillon Roger-Gaudry
facts: Its Art Deco tower, designed by Ernest Cormier, can be seen from all over the campus and the mountain.
It was called the Main Pavilion until 2003, when it was renamed after a former rector.

landmarks.name: Pavillon Marie-Victorin
facts: It is named after the botanist who founded the Montreal Botanical Garden.

landmarks.name: Pavillons Lassonde
facts: They belong to Polytechnique, the university's affiliated school of engineering.

landmarks.name: Pavillon Samuel-Bronfman;Bibliothèque des lettres et sciences humaines
facts: It houses the library for the humanities and social sciences.

landmarks.name: Pavillon André-Aisenstadt
facts: It houses the computer science department and a mathematics research centre.

landmarks.name: Pavillon Lionel-Groulx
facts: It is named after a priest and historian of French Canada.

landmarks.name: Pavillon Jean-Coutu
facts: It houses the Faculty of Pharmacy and is named after the founder of a Quebec drugstore chain.

landmarks.name: Pavillon Maximilien-Caron
facts: It is home to the Faculty of Law.
It took its current name in 1978, in honour of a jurist.
